history.dynasty: Disputed - Eastern Chalukya (per Wikipedia) vs Krimikantha Chola (per pilgrimage sources)
history.period: 15th century CE established; inscriptions suggest earlier origins
history.summary: CSV town 'Guntur' is approximate - the temple is in Bapatla town, now headquarters of its own Bapatla district (carved out of Guntur district in 2022). The town's name derives from this temple (Bhavanarayana-pattana -> Bapatla). Dated to the 15th century CE, it is a centrally protected monument of national importance (ASI). Origin is disputed: Wikipedia credits Vengi Chalukya ruler Kubja Vishnuvardhana; pilgrimage sources credit king Krimikantha Chola (1465) with a renovation by Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu in 1856. The Dravida-style gopuram was sculpted from a single rock, and the walls carry Telugu, Tamil and Sanskrit inscriptions - verify the conflicting claims with the ASI monument list.

name: Bhavanarayana Swamy Temple, Bapatla
town_description: Bapatla is a coastal town in southern Andhra Pradesh, headquarters of Bapatla district since the 2022 reorganization. It takes its name from the Bhavanarayana temple (Bhavanarayana-pattana). Known as an education hub with the Agricultural College, it lies about 49 km south of Guntur, near Suryalanka beach on the Bay of Bengal.

travel.road: Frequent APSRTC buses from Guntur, Vijayawada and Chirala; bus stand ~3 km from the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October-February; winter is most comfortable for coastal Andhra
visitor_information.opening_hours: Conflicting sources: prayanamam.com lists 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00 PM-8:00 PM; managudi.in lists 6:00 AM-9:00 PM - verify on arrival
